counting_rule: - **Your family, and when a round counts.** Record your model family relative to the builders' family as `same` or
`different`. A round counts toward convergence (`holon audit converge`, rules CV1-CV4) only if all of these hold, and
`holon audit round` refuses a round that sets `counts_toward_convergence` true without them (RD1, RD2):
- its family is `different`, or it is `same` and its `auditor.ruling` is exactly "HUMAN_ANSWERS Q9b" (the human's
ruling; spec/M3/lib/audit_rulings.json); a round so admitted keeps family `same`;
- every auditor type A1, A2, A3 and A4 ran;
- its auditor session is one no earlier round of M3 used (a fresh context, L19);
- it is not a dry run;
- it carries its evidence (spec/M3/lib/audit_evidence.json): its directory `audit/rounds/M3/round<n>/` holds each
record below, a JSON object that
- `a1.json` carries `a1_version` and names the round's milestone, number and target commit; is cited in the evidence
of an attack that ran with auditor type A1; has at least one of its `mutations` that ran, with a verdict other
than refused.
- `a2.json` carries `a2_version` and names the round's milestone, number and target commit; is cited in the evidence
of an attack that ran with auditor type A2; has at least one of its `cases` that ran, with a verdict other than
unsupported.
- `a4.json` carries `a4_version` and names the round's milestone, number and target commit; is cited in the evidence
of an attack that ran with auditor type A4; is valid against `spec/M3/lib/audit_a4.schema.json`; has exactly the
laws of `packet.json`; has `counts` that are the tally of its laws' `class`.
- `packet.json` carries `packet_version` and names the round's milestone, number and target commit; is the round's
`packet.path`, with that `sha256`; is valid against `spec/M3/lib/audit_packet.schema.json`; holds at least 1
law(s).
The lead rebuilds a4.json and packet.json from the round's target commit (`holon audit vacuity --milestone M3 --round
9 --check` and `holon audit hostile --milestone M3 --round 9 --check`); a record that does not rebuild byte for byte
is not evidence.
A round that does not count is still recorded, and its high-priority findings still reset the streak.
